draft.title: Amplitude, wavelength and frequency
card: Amplitude
the height of a wave above its rest position. A bigger amplitude means the wave carries more energy.
Wavelength
the distance from one peak to the next peak. It is measured in metres (m).
Frequency
the number of waves that pass a point each second. It is measured in hertz (Hz), where 1 Hz is one wave per second.
Wave speed = frequency × wavelength. So a wave with a frequency of 5 Hz and a wavelength of 2 m travels at 10 m/s.

1.alt: A wave with amplitude 2 and wavelength 4. The wave rises 2 units above the rest line at x = 1 and falls 2 units below it at x = 3. The distance between two neighbouring peaks, at x = 1 and x = 5, is marked as the wavelength. The amplitude is marked from the rest line down to the trough at x = 3.

draft.remember: Amplitude is height, wavelength is peak to peak, frequency is waves per second, and speed = frequency × wavelength.

a.q: Two waves travel along the same rope. Wave X has a larger amplitude than wave Y. What does this tell you about wave X?
opts: Its peaks rise higher above the rest position
More of its waves pass a point each second
It travels faster along the rope
a.why: Amplitude is the height of a wave above its rest position, so a larger amplitude means higher peaks. Wavelength is the distance between peaks, which is a different measure, so it does not describe amplitude.
a.clue: Amplitude is about height, not distance along the rope.

b.q: Waves pass a jetty in Lorne at a frequency of 0.5 Hz. The distance between neighbouring wave peaks is 8 m. What is the speed of the waves?
b.why: Wave speed = frequency × wavelength = 0.5 × 8 = 4 m/s. Dividing the wavelength by the frequency gives 16 m/s, which is a tempting mistake, but the card says to multiply.
b.clue: The distance between neighbouring peaks is the wavelength.
